steps.title: Establish primary fibroblast culture
steps.instruction: Grow primary fibroblast cells (derived from skin biopsies of volunteers F1, F2, F3) in a Corning® T25 flask containing Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM, 5 mM glucose, Gibco®) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS), 1 % penicillin (100 U mL⁻¹) / streptomycin (100 µg mL⁻¹), and 0.1 % amphotericin B (1 mg mL⁻¹). Incubate at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ atmosphere and change the culture medium every other day.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescent dye stock solutions
steps.instruction: Generate stock solutions as listed in Table 2: dissolve Hoechst 33342 in water to 5 mM; prepare MITO‑ID® Red stock in DMSO and dilute 10,000‑fold; dissolve MitoPY1 in methanol, aliquot, vacuum‑evaporate the solvent, and re‑dissolve freshly in DMSO to 10 mM for each experiment; dissolve JC‑10 in DMSO to 3 mM. Store stocks as indicated.

steps.title: Stain cells after stress treatment
steps.instruction: After applying the desired stress inducers, wash cells twice with PBS. Prepare a dye‑mix in phenol‑free DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS using the final concentrations from Table 2 (Hoechst 33342 3 µM, MITO‑ID® Red 10 µM, MitoPY1 10 µM, JC‑10 10 µM). Add 50 µL of this mixture to each well of a 96‑well plate and incubate for 30–45 min in the dark. Wash cells twice with PBS, then replace with phenol‑free DMEM containing 2 % FBS to reduce background before imaging.

steps.title: Acquire images with Operetta CLS
steps.instruction: Use the PerkinElmer Operetta CLS High‑Content Analysis System with a water‑immersion 40× high‑NA objective. Set binning to 2, temperature to 37 °C, CO₂ to 5 %, and capture images at 0.299 µm pixel size, 16‑bit depth, 1080 × 1080 pixels. For JC‑10 (mitochondrial membrane potential) use non‑confocal mode; for all other dyes use confocal mode. Capture 15–40 cells per field, 60–80 fields per well, and 2 wells per condition (≈ thousands of cells total).

substeps.instruction: Hoechst 33342: set mode to confocal and non‑confocal, exposure 300 ms, power 51 %, excitation 0 nm, excitation filter 53 nm, emission 65 nm, emission filter 35‑385 nm.
MITO‑ID® Red: confocal mode, exposure 1,300 ms, power 100 %, excitation 550 nm, excitation filter 530‑560 nm, emission 680 nm, emission filter 655‑705 nm.
MitoPY1: confocal mode, exposure 1,500 ms, power 100 %, excitation 510 nm, excitation filter 490‑515 nm, emission 553 nm, emission filter 525‑580 nm.
JC‑10 (Rhodamine): non‑confocal mode, exposure 555 ms, power 50 %, excitation 530‑560 nm, emission 610‑570 nm, emission filter 650 nm.
JC‑10 (Alexa 488): non‑confocal mode, exposure 510 ms, power 47 %, excitation 460‑490 nm, emission 525 nm, emission filter 500‑550 nm.

steps.title: Export images and extract metadata
steps.instruction: Upload the captured images to the Columbus program, export them, and extract metadata from each filename using the regular expression ^(?P<Plate>[0-9]{3})(?P<Well>[0-9]{3})-(?P<Site>[0-9]{1,2})-(?P<Channel>[0-9]{3})(?P<Time>[0-9]{3})(?P<Other>[0-9]{3})\.tif. Ensure each channel image is treated as a grayscale (single‑intensity) file.

steps.title: Analyze images with CellProfiler
steps.instruction: Load the exported images into CellProfiler (version 3.1.9 or 4.0.7). Use a pipeline that identifies nuclei (Hoechst 33342) and quantifies H₂O₂ (MitoPY1), J‑aggregates/J‑monomers (JC‑10), and mitochondrial granularity and length (MITO‑ID® Red). Run the pipeline to obtain measurements for each well.
